generation.hypothesis: The introduction of interstitial elements, such as oxygen or nitrogen, into high-entropy alloys can improve their resistance to thermally induced toughness loss by forming ordered interstitial complexes that impede dislocation motion and enhance strain hardening.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy in a demanding engineering application
generation.intervention: Introduction of interstitial elements, such as oxygen or nitrogen
generation.conditions: Elevated temperatures, similar to those in demanding engineering applications
generation.mechanism: Snoek relaxation and solid-solution strengthening, derived from materials-science principles
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, with a predicted increase in yield strength and elongation
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing route of the high-entropy alloy may affect the outcome, and further research is needed to fully understand the mechanism

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and damping measurements of high-entropy alloys with and without interstitial elements at elevated temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of interstitial elements does not result in improved resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, the hypothesis is falsified

System: Nb23.8Ta25.5Ti24.9V25.8 (nominally Nb25Ta25Ti25V25) BCC refractory high-entropy alloy. Processing: Arc melting under argon atmosphere from 99.99 wt% purity elements, melted 10 times, drop-cast into 4-mm diameter rods, homogenized at 1200°C for 3 days, followed by water cooling. Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy alloys be designed to simultaneously achieve high Snoek-type damping capacity, high mechanical strength, and high ductility at elevated temperatures?. System: Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi base HEA, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 (O-2 HEA), and (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98N2 (N-2 HEA). Processing: Arc-melting of pure metals (purity >99.9 wt%), TiN (99.9 wt%), and TiO2 (99.9 wt%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere; remelted at least eight times; drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold (10 mm × 10 mm × 60 mm).
